candidates.attacker_control: Unauthenticated remote attacker controls the request query parameters "loc" and "ln" (and the resource path segment after /javax.faces.resource/). Example shape: GET <faces-mapping>/javax.faces.resource/web.xml?loc=../WEB-INF — "loc" is returned unmodified by getLocalePrefixForLocateResource() and becomes the leading path segment of the resource identifier; "ln" is used the same way as the library-name segment. The resource path segment itself is normally normalized by the servlet container, which is why the traversal must be supplied through the query parameters.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked the suffix filter isResourceIdentifierExcluded()/RESOURCE_EXCLUDES (ResourceHandlerImpl.java:288-292, 486-505): it runs on the raw request path (/javax.faces.resource/web.xml), so it does not stop the traversal and does not block XML; .properties/.class/.jsp/.xhtml/.jspx remain blocked in the straightforward case. Checked the resource cache: ResourceHandlerCache keys include localePrefix, so a crafted "loc" is not served from a benign cached entry (ResourceHandlerCache.java:58-103). Checked the loader chain for any canonicalization: ExternalContextResourceLoader, ClassLoaderResourceLoader and ResourceMetaImpl contain only concatenation, no normalization or ".." checks (searched the whole tree for contains(".."), startsWith(".."), indexOf(".."), normalize() — the only normalize() hits are unrelated coercion/view-id logic). Checked the "ln" directory variant: on containers whose getResourcePaths() returns paths normalized against the context root, getLibraryVersion()'s resourcePath.substring(path.length()) (ExternalContextResourceLoader.java:79) can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, i.e. a 500 rather than a read; the "loc" variant ending in the resource file name avoids that branch because getResourcePaths() returns null for a file. Noted the traversal cannot escape the context root where the container rejects paths that normalize above the web-app root, so read scope is bounded to web-app contents.
candidates.impact: Unauthenticated information disclosure: arbitrary read of files that reside inside the deployed web application and are not blocked by the .class/.jsp/.jspx/.properties/.xhtml suffix filter — notably /WEB-INF/web.xml, /WEB-INF/faces-config.xml, WEB-INF/classes and other XML/text configuration, which commonly contain database credentials, JNDI/resource references and internal endpoint information. No write, code execution or cross-user impact was established from source; the "ln" variant can additionally produce an unhandled exception (denial-of-service style 500) when the loader iterates normalized directory entries (see counterevidence).
candidates.prerequisites: Standard JSF 2.0 web application using the default ResourceHandler with the FacesServlet mapped (e.g. /faces/* or *.jsf), so that ResourceHandler.handleResourceRequest() is reachable. The container's ServletContext.getResource()/getResourceAsStream() must resolve "../" segments within the context root instead of rejecting them (typical of Tomcat-style RequestUtil normalization: "/resources/../WEB-INF/web.xml" -> "/WEB-INF/web.xml", which stays inside the web-app root and is therefore allowed). The requested file must exist and must not end with one of the excluded suffixes (.class .jsp .jspx .properties .xhtml) — XML configuration files such as /WEB-INF/web.xml, /WEB-INF/faces-config.xml or /WEB-INF/classes/*.xml qualify.
candidates.root_cause: ResourceHandlerImpl trusts request parameters as path components. getLocalePrefixForLocateResource() (impl/.../ResourceHandlerImpl.java:436-450) reads the request parameter "loc" and returns it verbatim when non-null, with no charset/path validation, although the documented contract for loc is a locale prefix generated from ResourceHandler.LOCALE_PREFIX. handleResourceRequest() (lines 259-319) likewise takes libraryName from the raw "ln" parameter and resourceName from the request path, and the only rejection control, isResourceIdentifierExcluded(), matches file suffixes on the raw request path (lines 288-292, 486-505), not on the resolved target. deriveResourceMeta() (lines 132-241) then concatenates prefix/library/resource names with '/' and hands the resulting string to ResourceLoader.getResourceURL()/getResourceInputStream(); ResourceMetaImpl.getResourceIdentifier() (shared/.../ResourceMetaImpl.java:72-109) rebuilds the same unvalidated identifier, and ExternalContextResourceLoader.getResourceURL()/getResourceInputStream() (shared/.../ExternalContextResourceLoader.java:139-158) prepend the fixed "/resources" prefix and call ExternalContext.getResource()/getResourceAsStream(), i.e. ServletContext methods that normalize "../" segments. No layer performs canonicalization, ".." rejection, or containment checking against the resource root, so the traversal segments supplied in the query string survive into the container resource lookup and, if the resulting path is still inside the context root (e.g. /WEB-INF/...), the container returns the file and handleResourceRequest streams it to the client (lines 333-365).
candidates.title: Unauthenticated path traversal / web-app file read via ResourceHandler 'loc' (and 'ln') request parameters
candidates.trace: 1) FacesServlet.service() (api/src/main/java/javax/faces/webapp/FacesServlet.java:176-183) calls ResourceHandler.isResourceRequest(), which matches when the request path info starts with "/javax.faces.resource" (ResourceHandlerImpl.java:404-434). 2) handleResourceRequest() strips the identifier prefix to get resourceName (e.g. "web.xml"), reads libraryName from the "ln" parameter, and calls createResource() (ResourceHandlerImpl.java:294-319); the only filter, isResourceIdentifierExcluded(), tests the suffix of the un-resolved request path. 3) createResource() calls getLocalePrefixForLocateResource(), which returns the raw "loc" parameter value (e.g. "../WEB-INF") with no validation (ResourceHandlerImpl.java:94, 436-450). 4) deriveResourceMeta() concatenates localePrefix + '/' + resourceName ("../WEB-INF/web.xml") and validates existence via loader.getResourceURL() (ResourceHandlerImpl.java:171-187). 5) ExternalContextResourceLoader.getResourceURL()/getResourceInputStream() issue ExternalContext.getResource()/getResourceAsStream("/resources" + '/' + "../WEB-INF/web.xml") (ExternalContextResourceLoader.java:140-158), which delegates to ServletContext.getResource()/getResourceAsStream() (impl/.../ServletContextImplBase:118-129), where "../" is normalized and the file under /WEB-INF is returned. 6) handleResourceRequest() sets the content type and streams the resolved bytes to the HTTP response (ResourceHandlerImpl.java:333-365). The same unvalidated concatenation applies to "ln" (library name).
candidates.unverified: No runtime execution or container test was performed (tools are read-only; no build/deploy). The decisive environmental assumption — that the target container's ServletContext.getResource()/getResourceAsStream() normalize "/resources/../WEB-INF/<file>" to "/WEB-INF/<file>" and return it rather than null — is inferred from common Tomcat-style normalization in the MyFaces 2.0.x era and was not verified here; on containers that reject any path containing "..", the same code path yields 404 instead. It is also unverified whether the missing validation is an intentionally modified defect or the historical upstream state of MyFaces 2.0.11 (no upstream copy or patch history is available in the snapshot), and the served content type/body of the retrieved file was not observed.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal'); CWE-20 missing input validation on request parameter used in resource path

coverage_summary: All 1173 model-visible files (api, impl, shared, implee6, integration-tests; ~589 impl, ~120 shared, ~330 api files) were enumerated and filtered only by the standard binary/size/symlink policy (0 excluded). Search sweeps covered dangerous sinks (Runtime.exec, ObjectInputStream, new File/File streams, Class.forName, URL.openConnection, DocumentBuilderFactory, setAccessible, Cipher, Pattern.compile), all request-parameter reads (getRequestParameterMap/getParameter) and their uses, escaping utilities (HTMLEncoder, HtmlResponseWriterImpl, HtmlJavaScriptUtils, JstlFunction, ErrorPageWriter), view-state handling (StateUtils, HtmlResponseStateManager, ServerSideStateCacheImpl, ClientSideStateCacheImpl, Jsp/DefaultFacelets state helpers), resource handling (ResourceHandlerImpl, ResourceMetaImpl, ResourceImpl, all ResourceLoader implementations, ResourceHandlerCache, ResourceUtils), external context/servlet wrappers, navigation/view handling, flash scope, and sampled client-side JS (48 files: eval/innerHTML/document.write handlers). Deep-read in full: the resource-handling chain used for the finding, StateUtils, MyFacesObjectInputStream, HtmlResponseWriterImpl (key methods), HTMLEncoder, ExternalContextResourceLoader, ClassLoaderResourceLoader, BaseResourceHandlerSupport, ResourceMetaImpl, ResourceImpl, FlashImpl (key sections), PartialResponseWriterImpl (partially), UIDebug, FacesServlet, SourceCodeServlet, DefaultRestoreViewSupport, Path, DefaultFaceletFactory (key methods), MyFacesConfig flag parsing, WebConfigParamUtils, ResourceHandlerCache, HtmlAjaxBehaviorRenderer, HtmlLinkRendererBase.decode, oamSubmit.js. Not read line-by-line: FaceletViewDeclarationLanguage (105 KB), DefaultFaceletsStateManagementStrategy (55 KB), ApplicationImpl (99 KB), HtmlRendererUtils (120 KB), JspStateManagerImpl (47 KB), ErrorPageWriter (55 KB, sampled), AnnotationConfigurator (40 KB) and most api-module component/renderer classes; these remain partial-coverage areas where additional (mainly hardening-level) issues could exist.
limitations: Read-only review: no build, deployment, test execution or runtime confirmation was possible; the candidate is a source-level lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.

Cannot inspect upstream MyFaces 2.0.11 or later fix commits, so I cannot distinguish an introduced defect from historical upstream code; the finding is based on the absence of any validation in the snapshot itself.

The exploitability hinges on container-specific ServletContext path normalization, which was reasoned about but not verified; behavior differs across Tomcat/Jetty/other containers and across versions.
No unit or integration tests are present in the snapshot for the resource handling path, so expected/forbidden behavior could not be corroborated from tests.

Large files (HtmlRendererUtils, FaceletViewDeclarationLanguage, ApplicationImpl, DefaultFaceletsStateManagementStrategy, JspStateManagerImpl, AnnotationConfigurator) and most client-side JavaScript were only sampled, so coverage there is incomplete.
Search-based review can miss issues that do not use the searched sink/keyword patterns (e.g., logic/authorization defects expressed through ordinary method calls).

rejected_leads.lead: Insecure deserialization of the client-supplied javax.faces.ViewState (shared/.../StateUtils.java reconstruct() -> getAsObject() -> ObjectInputStream.readObject() via MyFacesObjectInputStream, which has no class allow-list; shared/.../MyFacesObjectInputStream.java:36-56).
rejected_leads.reason: Source evidence is strong, but reachability as a default configuration is weak: MyFaces enables encryption+HMAC by default (StateUtils.isSecure() returns true unless org.apache.myfaces.USE_ENCRYPTION=false), so the state is authenticated and the bytes cannot be forged; server-side state saving is the spec default. Exploitation would require the operator to switch to client-side state saving and disable encryption (two non-default settings), so this was treated as a configuration-dependent hardening issue rather than the strongest finding.

rejected_leads.lead: EL evaluation of served CSS resources: ResourceImpl.getInputStream() wraps any text/css resource in ValueExpressionFilterInputStream, which parses "#{...}" from file content and evaluates it with createValueExpression()/getValue() (shared/.../ResourceImpl.java:76-215).
rejected_leads.reason: The evaluator is real and unconditional, but the attacker does not control the CSS content through the framework alone: exploitation requires the application to place attacker-influenced CSS into a path served by the ResourceHandler (e.g. an upload/CM feature). No such attacker-controlled write path was identified in this repository, so the injection precondition is external.

rejected_leads.lead: UIDebug.debugRequest() writes previously captured debug output (component tree/session attributes) to the response when the facelets.ui.DebugOutput request parameter is present (impl/.../tag/ui/UIDebug.java:179-205).
rejected_leads.reason: The debug output is fetched from the current request's own session map by id (fetchDebugOutput), so an attacker can only retrieve data already stored in their own session; ids are per-JVM sequential but that does not cross the session boundary. No cross-user disclosure established.

rejected_leads.lead: SourceCodeServlet prints the JSP source of the requested *.source path (shared/.../util/servlet/SourceCodeServlet.java:25-61).
rejected_leads.reason: It is a developer/example servlet that is not registered by MyFaces itself (no web.xml or annotation mapping in this snapshot), so it is unreachable unless an application deliberately maps it. Treated as a deployment hazard, not a framework vulnerability.
A real copy/paste defect, but the impact is limited to possible NullPointerException for unusual request/response type combinations; no attacker-controlled security decision depends on it.

rejected_leads.lead: Error/debug page rendering (ErrorPageWriter._writeVariables) only escapes '<' in keys/values (impl/.../renderkit/ErrorPageWriter.java:762-819).
rejected_leads.reason: Values are written in HTML text context where replacing '<' prevents tag injection; the debug/error page is only produced in Development project stage (or when org.apache.myfaces.ERROR_HANDLING is explicitly enabled). No concrete breakout was identified, so this stays a hardening/robustness observation.

summary: Reviewed the Apache MyFaces Core 2.0.11 snapshot (1173 files: api, impl, shared, implee6, integration-tests). Best-supported finding: the default JSF ResourceHandler builds resource lookup paths directly from the attacker-controlled "loc" and "ln" request parameters without any normalization/allow-list validation, so a relative path such as loc=../WEB-INF lets a resource request resolve outside /resources and serve files under /WEB-INF (path traversal / arbitrary web-app file read). Traced the full flow across files: FacesServlet.service -> ResourceHandlerImpl.handleResourceRequest (reads ln, derives resourceName from path info, only suffix-filters the request path) -> ResourceHandlerImpl.getLocalePrefixForLocateResource (returns the raw "loc" parameter) -> deriveResourceMeta (string concatenation localePrefix/libraryName/resourceName) -> ResourceMetaImpl.getResourceIdentifier -> ExternalContextResourceLoader.getResourceURL/getResourceInputStream -> ExternalContext/ServletContext.getResource("/resources/../WEB-INF/..."). Impact is unauthenticated disclosure of web-app files that pass the extension filter (web.xml, *-config.xml, *.xml/*.txt under WEB-INF or WEB-INF/classes), which often contain credentials/JNDI/resource configuration. Only one candidate is submitted; other plausible-but-weaker leads are listed as rejected.
